title: Double-click and two people editing the same quotation

steps.do: "+ New quote", fill a valid quotation, double-click "Create quote".
steps.expect: One quotation is created. If the form is sent twice you see "That quote was already saved — here it is."
steps.observed: One quotation after the double-click; sending the same form again created nothing and said "That was already saved — the form was sent twice, so the second copy was ignored.".
steps.note: Sending the same form again is caught by the app-wide double-send guard first, which says "That was already saved — the form was sent twice, so the second copy was ignored." (landing on /quote?id=1), not the quotation's own "That quote was already saved — here it is."
steps.suggest: If the form is sent twice you are told it was already saved, and no second quotation is made.

steps.do: Two people open "Edit" on the same draft. A changes Contact person and saves. B then changes Subject and saves.
steps.expect: B is refused: "Someone else saved changes to this record while you had it open. Reopen it to see the latest version, then re-apply your change — your edit was not saved, so nothing of theirs was overwritten." A's change is kept.
steps.observed: A (Test BDM) saved ("Quote saved."); B (admin) was refused: "Someone else saved changes to this record while you had it open. Reopen it to se…"; A's contact person is kept and the subject is unchanged.
steps.note: B is the Master Admin here: since 14 Nov 2026 a quotation assigned to Test BDM is edited only by Test BDM and the people above them, so a second sales colleague cannot open its Edit screen.
